questions.q: What does a Failover Cluster Instance (FCI) actually protect, per this lesson?
options: The SQL Server instance itself — not individual databases the way an Availability Group does
Individual databases, replicated to every cluster node
Only the tempdb database
Client applications, not the server side at all
questions.explain: An FCI is one single SQL Server instance that runs on whichever node is active; it isn't database-level replication like an AG.

questions.q: How many copies of the data and log files exist in an FCI setup?
options: One — on shared storage that every node can access, not a copy per node
One copy per cluster node, kept in sync
Two: one for the active node, one for the passive node
It depends on the number of databases
questions.explain: There's no replication in an FCI. There's a single set of data/log files on shared storage; only the running instance's location changes on failover.

questions.q: What is a 'passive' node doing while another node is active in an FCI cluster?
options: Standing by with SQL Server installed, but not running against the data or storage
Actively serving read-only queries against a copy of the database
Continuously copying transaction log records from the active node
Running a completely different SQL Server instance
questions.explain: Passive nodes have SQL Server installed but idle; they only start running the instance if WSFC fails the resource group over to them.

questions.q: Why does a client application not need to know which physical node is currently active in an FCI?
options: It connects to a stable virtual network name (VNN) that moves with the active node
SQL Server automatically emails the client the new node's IP address
FCIs don't support client connections at all
The client must be manually reconfigured after every failover
questions.explain: Clients connect to the FCI's virtual network name, which WSFC keeps pointed at whichever node is currently active.

questions.q: A colleague says an FCI means databases are 'replicated across three nodes for safety.' What's wrong with that statement?
options: An FCI doesn't replicate anything — there's one copy of the data on shared storage that different nodes take turns running against
Nothing is wrong; that's exactly what an FCI does
FCIs only ever use a single node, never more than one
FCIs replicate the instance but not the databases
questions.explain: This is the core misconception this lesson corrects: FCIs are active/passive over shared storage, not replication across nodes.
